name: the-tavern
description: The Tavern — a crew of AI builders for Claude Code. Sage draws it. Smith builds it.

plugins.name: sage
plugins.description: Codebase-aware specification engine for Claude Code. Runs parallel codebase research, then a grounded interview that captures implicit facts as A-AUTO-NNN entries, emits typed Global Invariants / State Transitions / Contracts tables, runs an adversarial spec review at R3.5, then writes a Smith-ready spec with version frontmatter (v2.1) — locked, classified, citation-backed. Detects brownfield, greenfield, and cosmetic modes; brownfield runs produce a flow delta against the existing system. Sage plans. Smith builds.

plugins.name: smith
plugins.description: Smith is the builder on the The Tavern crew — an autonomous build-verify-fix loop for Claude Code. Smith reads Sage's spec, decomposes it into castings with pre-authored teammate prompts, validates through an 11-dimension M0.9 gate (including M0.7 intent-carrier coverage), builds in parallel waves with server-side evidence re-execution and per-requirement-ID binding, runs up to 8 verification streams (TRACE, FLOW_TRACE, PROVE, RESEARCH_AUDIT, COVERAGE_DIFF, SIGHT, TEST/PROBE, TEST_OBSERVATIONS), grinds defects to zero, then assays with fresh eyes. Brownfield runs consume a flow delta; greenfield and cosmetic runs use the end-state pipeline. Sage draws it. Smith builds it.

plugins.name: warden
plugins.description: Warden keeps every job plumb, level, and true — measure twice, cut once. He stops Claude from racing on ad-hoc work. Methodical-mode pre-response checklist injected every turn (Restate, Verified/Unverified assumptions, Read Floor, Approach Deliberation, Blast Radius, Stall Check, Competing Hypotheses, Goal-Driven Execution, See It Through, Observation Grounding). Stop hook enforces five gates: file:line citation verifier, uncertainty-tell scanner, Fable-mode completion gate (blocks responses that end by promising first-person work without doing it), zero-tool-call grounding audit, and an iterative two-tier critic-dialog (Haiku fast-critic rounds 1-3, opus pre-stop-critic rounds 4-6, HARD block at round 6 until /warden:trust-me bypass). Each critic runs a 10-item rule compliance audit and sees the prior round's feedback to verify Claude actually addressed flagged issues. /warden:casual (one turn skip), /warden:trust-me (one-turn strict bypass), /warden:fable-off (disable completion gate), /warden:off (session disable). /warden:deep for heavier analysis, /warden:second-opinion for independent critique.

plugins.name: sellsword
plugins.description: Hand Sellsword a gnarly problem and he owns the outcome end to end. Sellsword is the general contractor: he runs a crew of five Opus sub-agents (dispatcher, recon, builder, auditor, fresh-eyes) to investigate, plan, execute, and verify — SSH into systems, spin up infra, edit code, ship features, debug deploys, get airgap bundles working. The builder self-switches between investigating, planning, executing, and verifying modes. Bounded recon budget, multi-angle retry on stuck (N=2-3 parallel variants + arbiter), and the auditor and fresh-eyes must each produce evidence ledgers of commands they actually ran. One checkpoint (plan approval) for side-effecting tasks, zero for pure investigation. Plan and debrief render in chat; state files live in .sellsword/runs/ for resume. /sellsword:goal runs the builder→auditor→fresh-eyes loop unattended until auditor and fresh-eyes both return pass — enforced by a Stop hook, bounded by cycle and time caps.

plugins.name: cleric
plugins.description: Cleric is the crew member who sweeps the site clean — careful, low-risk codebase cleanup across 7 focused tracks: deduplication, type consolidation, dead code removal, circular dependency untangling, type strengthening, error-handling cleanup, and deprecated/AI-slop removal. On each track Cleric inspects, writes a critical assessment, ranks proposed changes by confidence, and auto-applies ONLY HIGH-confidence LOW-risk changes per batch — running language-appropriate type checks, tests, and lints after each batch. MEDIUM and LOW confidence changes get surfaced for explicit human approval. Atomic commits per batch so any failing check is one git revert away. Cleric works the conservative cleanup pass — never merging code that just LOOKS similar, never removing dynamically-imported code, never breaking legitimate boundary types, never silencing real errors. Refuses to use comments as a source of truth.

plugins.name: scout
plugins.description: Scout is the inspector who tests every room — end-to-end test authoring and maintenance for web apps via Playwright + Playwright MCP. She drives a real browser, reads the accessibility tree, and emits *.spec.ts files that pass — then keeps them passing. /scout:init scaffolds Playwright in the cwd and registers the MCP server. /scout:write <flow> drives the browser to perform the flow and emits a green spec. /scout:crawl discovers every route and generates a smoke spec per route. /scout:matrix produces a routes × roles coverage suite with reused storageState. /scout:audit runs the suite, reads trace.zip files, and triages failures by root cause. /scout:record wraps playwright codegen for manual capture. The author skill enforces selector hygiene (getByRole over CSS), auto-wait discipline, and idempotent test design; the diagnose skill drives trace-driven flaky-test triage. The spec-writer subagent isolates MCP-driven spec authoring from the main context.

plugins.name: tactician
plugins.description: Generate really good dynamic Workflow scripts on demand. /tactician:make <task> classifies the task into an orchestration archetype (understand / design / review / research / migrate / generic), picks the right fan-out topology (pipeline by default, barrier only when a stage genuinely needs all prior results), and authors a self-contained Workflow script that obeys the Workflow tool's hard rules — pure-literal meta block, schema'd agent returns instead of text parsing, .filter(Boolean) after fan-out, adversarial-verify for findings, loop-until-dry / loop-until-budget for unknown-size work, isolation:'worktree' only for parallel file mutation, no Date.now/Math.random. Every script is validated with `node --check` and a 14-point self-audit before it is saved to .claude/workflows/ or run. Tactician rigs up the orchestration so you don't freehand it.

plugins.name: seer
plugins.description: Macro-architecture / design-cohesion review — the senior-engineer 'is this shaped right or accreted?' critique, not bug-hunting or lint. Seer reads a codebase the way a gumshoe reads a crime scene: deduces the real design problem from the detail that's out of place. /seer:review <target> runs a Workflow engine that builds a grounded structural map of the target (a path, the diff, a subsystem, or a described piece of logic), then runs 8 blind design lenses — package/module proliferation, missed sharing & reuse, helper sprawl & abstraction fit, flow & layering, cohesion, naming/structural consistency, accretion markers, boundary & dependency direction — each a separate agent hunting one class of design problem. Every candidate finding is adversarially cross-examined by a skeptic that tries to refute it as intentional, so plausible-but-wrong smells get dropped; a completeness critic then re-lenses any in-scope area no finding touched. The result is synthesized into a per-subsystem deliberate/mixed/accreted verdict with file:line evidence and an ordered, concrete reshaping plan. Report only — never edits code. Forbidden from style nits, correctness bugs, or treating comments as source of truth ('the code is the only witness that doesn't lie'); an empty result is a valid honest outcome for a well-shaped target.

plugins.name: ranger
plugins.description: Ranger is the foreman who never leaves the site. Give him one prompt and walk away — he runs a self-directing senior-engineering loop that never stops and never runs out of work. A thin lead (reads state files, never code) drives five Opus sub-agents — scout, planner, implementer, reviewer, assessor — through survey → rank → plan → plan-review → build → review → verify → commit, one local commit per item. When the backlog runs dry the scout steps back, enumerates the app's domains, and rotates through them with a persistent pointer — correctness, UI/UX and visual polish, real-user flows, performance, accessibility, security, feature gaps — so there is always work, and never a second pass over the same ground. UI items are driven through a real browser as a user would, then fixed and made to look better. Each invocation runs one cycle and returns; keep it going with `/loop /ranger:run` (watched, Esc to stop) or the bundled headless runner (overnight) — no Stop-hook trapping or transcript spam. Curated `--preset` briefs (ui, ux, a11y, harden, perf) focus the sweep and skip anything the app lacks instead of inventing it, and `--dry-run` previews the work without changing anything. A PreToolUse hook hard-denies git push, remote mutation, and PR creation regardless of what the model decides. Local commits only. Branches and dev merges require explicit flags. Never asks the user anything unless --ask. Blast-radius circuit breaker, no-progress quarantine, and revert-don't-pile-on regression discipline keep an unattended run from turning into churn.
